details:
My Suggestion is a more granular approach to performance ranking.

One of the biggest issues with the community, is that there is no obvious way to distinguish between someone who's avatar is barely Very Poor and someone who's, avatar is much worse.

For example someone with an avatar with 70,001 polys but nothing else wrong with the avatar, and someone with an avatar with 3 million polys, 200 mats, 100k particles and 1gb of VRAM usage both just show up as "Very Poor".

In an ideal world, everyone would just make Poor or better avatars, but if we want the community to start policing itself, the 2 people in my example shouldn't be lumped in together, and it makes it much more clear if a specific avatar is significantly worse than others, even if all avatars in a lobby are "Very Poor".

My suggestion for how to accomplish this is a weight system, so each part of an avatar, the polys, the materials, the phybones components, everything, have a number attached to it, representing how big of an impact it has to performance, and you would simply add these number up and display it. So for example, maybe a poor avatar that is maxed in every category but isnt Very Poor yet, would have a rank of 5k for example and anything higher would be very poor, it would then be easy to, at a glance, tell the difference between someone who's avatar is 6k and 20k or even 100k.

The ranks dont need to disappear, and VRChat would still only officially support for Poor or better avatars, but not only would this allow us to see avatars that are significantly worse, but community's now have a greater degree of control, so if they wanted, they could say, at this event no one use an avatar worse than 10k, which allows more freedom than just saying " avatars must be Poor or better", but also means, no one will wear something egregious, and those that do, can be spotted easily.
title: Granular Avatar Ranking
